---
title: "Top Parks Over Time"
subtitle: "Watch the ranking of the 10 busiest National Park Service units change from 2000 to 2025"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
toc: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup-top-parks
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

annual_visits <- read_csv(
  "nps_annual_visits_1979_2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= 2025)

# Keep the consistent pool of all parks that ever entered the top 10 so Plotly smoothly interpolates every bar
ever_top10 <- annual_visits |>
  group_by(year) |>
  slice_max(recreation_visits, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(park) |>
  unique()

top_by_year <- annual_visits |>
  filter(park %in% ever_top10) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(desc(recreation_visits))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(year, rank)
```

## Which parks lead the system?

Use the year slider to compare the **10 busiest reporting units**. The ranking is based on each year's total recreation visits, so annual counts are not adjusted for park size or number of days open.

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-parks
#| fig-cap: "The 10 National Park Service units with the highest reported recreation visitation in each year, 2000–2025."
#| column: page-inset

plot_ly(
  data = top_by_year,
  x = ~recreation_visits,
  y = ~rank,
  type = "bar",
  orientation = "h",
  height = 500,
  frame = ~year,
  ids = ~park,
  hovertext = ~paste0(
    "<b>#", rank, " · ", park, "</b><br>",
    scales::comma(recreation_visits), " visits in ", year
  ),
  hovertemplate = "%{hovertext}<extra></extra>",
  text = ~paste0(" ", park),
  textposition = "outside",
  cliponaxis = FALSE,
  textfont = list(color = "#1E382B", size = 12, family = "system-ui, sans-serif"),
  marker = list(
    color = "#2F6B48",
    line = list(color = "#1E382B", width = 1)
  )
) |>
  layout(
    paper_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    plot_bgcolor = "#FAF7F0",
    margin = list(l = 55, r = 190, t = 20, b = 55),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "Annual recreation visits",
      tickformat = "~s",
      gridcolor = "#E6E1D2",
      zeroline = FALSE,
      range = c(0, 23500000)
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "",
      autorange = FALSE,
      range = c(10.5, 0.5),
      tickmode = "array",
      tickvals = 1:10,
      ticktext = paste0("#", 1:10),
      fixedrange = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  animation_opts(
    frame = 1000,
    transition = 800,
    easing = "cubic-in-out",
    redraw = FALSE
  ) |>
  animation_slider(
    currentvalue = list(prefix = "Year: ", font = list(color = "#1E382B"))
  ) |>
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

## How to read this view

The order changes from year to year, but **Great Smoky Mountains, Blue Ridge Parkway, Golden Gate, and other high-volume units** often remain among the leaders. Because the plot uses an absolute visit count, a large urban or scenic recreation area can rank above a smaller National Park even though it may offer a very different visitor experience.
